fixes.explanation: That's the one, friend. Israel made Joseph a robe of many colors, and the text says Joseph was born to him in his old age. My favorite color is the rainbow because I can't pick just one, so I understand a robe that couldn't pick either. I'd have asked to borrow it for a batch day. (Genesis 37:3)

Twenty shekels of silver, you've got it, friend. The brothers pull Joseph out of the pit and sell him to the Ishmaelites, who take him to Egypt. Judah had told them, “Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites and not lay a hand on him…” I think this is one of the heavy parts of the story. (Genesis 37:27-28)

Wind never comes up in Joseph's telling, baker. He says, “…your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to mine.” The sheaves in his dream gather and bow. That's what he tells his brothers. (Genesis 37:7)

Not quite, friend. After Reuben tears his clothes, the text has him return to his brothers and say, “The boy is gone! What am I going to do?” The words go to his brothers. The text doesn't show him going to his father. (Genesis 37:29-30)

This one is true, friend. The brothers send the robe and ask Jacob to examine it and see whether it's his son's. Jacob knows it is, and he draws his own conclusion from it. I think it's a hard verse to sit with. (Genesis 37:32-33)
